subject: How to set a different value for mean and standard deviation

messages.author: f0d4c7c39276e09b
messages.subject: How to set a different value for mean and standard deviation
parts:
Hi Phil,

I'm working with a dataset provided by ENEM, a reference test for Brazilian students to take in order to apply for federal universities. They use as reference values 500 (mean) and 100 (standard deviation) for de scores. I would like to know how to change that and calculate the scores in that scale.


Thanks!!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: How to set a different value for mean and standard deviation
parts:
Could you describe how these reference values are used in a standard setting? Like, how this [500,100] property is achieved for a given sample in practice? Typically,  total scores are obtained on a test first then mean/variance shifted to reflect this general spread. Such things are also possible in IRT using factor scores, but I want to make sure my recommendation is in-line with what you are asking.

Phil

messages.author: f0d4c7c39276e09b
messages.subject: Re: How to set a different value for mean and standard deviation
parts:
Here's what they said on a technical note: 

No Enem, foi estabelecida uma escala em 2009 para possibilitar o acompanhamento e comparação do desempenho dos participantes ao longo dos anos. Da mesma forma que se convencionou a escala “metro” para mensuração do comprimento, estabeleceu-se para esta comparação, a escala “Enem”. Nessa escala, foram considerados os concluintes regulares de 2009 como grupo de referência, definindo-se a média desse grupo como 500 e seu desvio-padrão 100.

On ENEM was stablished a scale in 2009 to make possible the following and comparison the performance of the participants over the years. The same way that was agreed the meter scale for measuring length, it was stablished for this comparison, the scale "Enem". In this scale, it was considered the high school graduating as reference group, defining the mean of this group as 500 and its standard deviation 100.
I wanna know if it is possible for me to set that on the mirt package.


Thanks

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: How to set a different value for mean and standard deviation
parts:
Sure, but that doesn't really help me determine what one does in any given sample. For instance, you obtain the following total scores on the test:

[50,65,45,51,22]

How does one go about transforming this given set of observations into their mean of 500 sd of 100 form? If you had the full population data then you would know what the mean/sd of the population is, so rescaling is easy. Without knowing these properties it is not possible to rescale the observed vector of values with the same mean/sd shift to ensure the data were scaled around the defined population location. In other words, I could very easily rescale the above vector to have your properties, but these transformations are not guaranteed to match the original shift.

> ts <- c(50,65,45,51,22)
> scaled <- scale(ts) * 100 + 500
> mean(scaled)
[1] 500
> sd(scaled)
[1] 100

Phil
